identified_issues: Authorization policy Rule Set v4.2 fails to validate target resource operational state, violating lawful support boundaries and finite quotient admissibility.
Unconditioned authorization of destructive SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT operation against an active primary volume (PRIMARY_MODE) with active concurrent transactions and uncommitted dirty buffers.
Decoupling of role permissions from operational prerequisites allows catastrophic state overwrite and potential data corruption.
evidence: Volume operating mode specifications define SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT as supported only in STANDBY_MODE, with an explicit constraint barring execution when active transactional writes or uncommitted buffers exist.
VOL_481 is actively operating in PRIMARY_MODE, processing live customer database writes and maintaining uncommitted memory buffers.
Authorization middleware approved request POST /api/v1/volumes/VOL_481/actions with action SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT solely based on VOLUME_OPERATOR role membership without checking operational mode.
Destructive snapshot overwrite was scheduled for execution on active primary volume VOL_481.
recommended_action: Immediately abort and revoke the scheduled SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT execution on VOL_481. Revert Rule Set v4.2 authorization middleware to enforce target operational state preconditions, restricting SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT admissibility strictly to validated STANDBY_MODE volumes.
